Distribution. The species C. jaliscoensis sp. n., is known from pine and oak forests in the Sierra del Tigre of Jalisco. It may be present in areas with similar vegetation such as the Sierra de Manantlán, Volcán Nevado de Colima, and western part of Transmexican Volcanic Belt (Fig. 57).

Distribution and Biology. This species has been recorded only from islands in the Bahamas. Adults were captured in March – June. Larval hosts are unknown. Specimens were collected in open disturbed areas less than 0.1 mile from the shoreline with dune vegetation present.
